definition: to admit that something is true, or to show that you have received something
examples: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.
She acknowledged my email within the hour.

definition: to change your behaviour or a thing so that it fits a new situation
examples: Children adapt to new schools quickly.
The recipe was adapted for a smaller oven.

definition: easy to see or understand, or seeming true without being certain
examples: It soon became apparent that we were lost.
There was no apparent reason for the delay.

definition: a way of dealing with a problem or a task
examples: They took a careful approach to the repair.
Her approach to teaching is unusual.

definition: to accept that something is true without checking it
examples: I assumed the shop was open.
Do not assume that everyone agrees.

definition: a good result that you get from something
examples: Regular sleep has clear benefits.
The benefits outweighed the cost.

definition: to decide something after thinking about the facts, or to bring something to an end
examples: The report concluded that the road was unsafe.
She concluded her talk with a question.

definition: to think about something carefully before deciding
examples: We are considering two options.
Consider how much time it will take.

definition: staying the same over time, or not containing contradictions
examples: His work is consistent in quality.
Her answer was consistent with the evidence.

definition: to have something inside, or to keep something from spreading
examples: The box contained old photographs.
Firefighters contained the blaze by morning.

definition: to make someone believe something or agree to do something
examples: He convinced me to try again.
The argument did not convince the committee.

definition: a strong request, or the amount of something that people want to buy
examples: Demand for the book was higher than expected.
The union made three demands.

definition: to be decided by something else, or to need someone for support
examples: The answer depends on the weather.
Small farms depend on rain.

definition: to find out something exactly, or to control what something will be
examples: Tests determined the cause of the leak.
Rainfall determines the size of the harvest.

definition: special importance given to one thing rather than others
examples: The course places emphasis on speaking.
She put emphasis on the second word.

definition: to start something that is meant to last, or to prove that something is true
examples: The school was established in 1902.
Police established that he had left earlier.

definition: facts that make you believe that something is true
examples: There is little evidence for that claim.
The evidence points the other way.

definition: to work something out after thinking about it
examples: I could not figure out the instructions.
She figured the trip would take two hours.

definition: happening slowly over a long period rather than suddenly
examples: There was a gradual rise in temperature.
Recovery was gradual but steady.

definition: to say who or what someone or something is
examples: Can you identify the man in this photograph?
The study identified three main causes.

definition: a strong effect that one thing has on another
examples: The new rule had little impact on traffic.
Her speech made an impact.

definition: to show that something is probably true, or to point something out
examples: The results indicate a small rise.
He indicated the door with a nod.

definition: to keep something in the same state, or to keep saying that something is true
examples: It is hard to maintain that speed.
He maintains that he was elsewhere.

definition: to get something, often after some effort
examples: She obtained a copy of the report.
Permission must be obtained first.

definition: to happen, especially without being planned
examples: The fault occurs only in cold weather.
It never occurred to me to ask.

definition: used to say what would happen if something were not done
examples: Write it down; otherwise you will forget.
The room was cold but otherwise fine.

definition: the result of a process or an event
examples: Nobody could predict the outcome.
The outcome surprised the researchers.

definition: to take part in an activity together with others
examples: Forty schools participated in the study.
She rarely participates in discussion.

definition: coming before the one being talked about
examples: See the previous chapter.
In previous years the river froze.

definition: not wanting to do something, and therefore slow to do it
examples: She was reluctant to leave so early.
He gave a reluctant nod.

definition: to need something, or to make something necessary by a rule
examples: The job requires patience.
All visitors are required to sign in.

definition: to make known something that was hidden
examples: The letter revealed his real reason.
Tests revealed no damage.

definition: large or important enough to be worth noticing
examples: There was a significant drop in sales.
She played a significant part in the project.

definition: to try hard to do something that is difficult
examples: He struggled to stay awake.
Small shops struggled through the winter.

definition: as much as is needed for a purpose
examples: We had sufficient time to prepare.
The evidence was not sufficient.

definition: to usually do a particular thing, or to usually be a particular way
examples: Prices tend to rise in summer.
He tends to speak quickly.

definition: to move someone or something from one place to another
examples: She transferred to a different office.
Transfer the money before Friday.

definition: a general direction in which something is changing
examples: The trend is towards shorter meetings.
Sales followed the same trend.

definition: to be different in different situations, or to change something on purpose
examples: Prices vary from shop to shop.
Vary the pace to hold attention.

definition: almost completely, but not quite
examples: The hall was virtually empty.
It is virtually impossible to prove.
